## Key Research Areas and Recent Developments (2024-2025)

**Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)**

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing large language models (LLMs) in reasoning tasks such as mathematics and code generation. Verifiable Rewards are simple functions that provide a clear-cut, binary ground truth signal - typically a "1" (correct) or "0" (incorrect) - to indicate whether a model's output meets a predefined correctness criterion.

**Reward Shaping and Code Generation**

The TEXT2REWARD framework generates and shapes dense reward code based on goal descriptions, using large language models grounded on a compact, Pythonic representation of the environment. The CARD framework is an LLM-driven Reward Design framework that generates and improves reward function code iteratively, with a Coder that generates and verifies the code, while an Evaluator provides dynamic feedback to improve the code.

**Formal Verification and Open-Ended Generation**

While RLVR succeeds in reasoning tasks by checking the final verifiable answer, extending this paradigm to open-ended generation is challenging because there is no unambiguous ground truth; RLVRR (reinforcement learning with verifiable reference-based rewards) addresses these issues.

**LLM-Based Reward Generation**

LLM-based reward generation methodologies can be organized along several axes: direct reward code synthesis, reward model learning, reward-guided search, and preference/rubric-based supervision.

Static program analysis is the analysis of computer programs performed without executing them, in contrast with dynamic program analysis, which is performed on programs during their execution. ## Overview

SATLM (Satisfiability-Aided Language Modeling) is an approach for improving the reasoning capabilities of LLMs that uses an LLM to generate a declarative task specification rather than an imperative program and leverages an off-the-shelf automated theorem prover to derive the final answer.

## Core Approach

The core idea is to cast a natural language (NL) reasoning problem as a satisfiability (SAT for short) problem. The LLM parses an NL query into a declarative specification and leverages a SAT solver to derive the final answer.

## Key Advantages

The declarative specification is closer to the problem description than the reasoning steps are, so the LLM can parse it out of the description more accurately. Furthermore, by offloading the actual reasoning task to an automated theorem prover, the approach can guarantee the correctness of the answer with respect to the parsed specification and avoid planning errors in the solving process.

## Performance Results

SATLM was evaluated on 8 different datasets and consistently outperforms program-aided LMs in the imperative paradigm. In particular, SATLM outperforms program-aided LMs by 23% on a challenging subset of the GSM arithmetic reasoning dataset; SATLM also achieves a new SoTA on LSAT and BoardgameQA, surpassing previous models that are trained on the respective training sets.

## Publication Details

The paper was published on arXiv as document 2305.09656 in May 2023, with the final version appearing in October 2023.

I found comprehensive information about MO-GRPO. Here's what the research shows:

## Overview

MO-GRPO is an extension of GRPO with a simple normalization method to reweight the reward functions automatically according to the variances of their values.

## Problem It Addresses

GRPO is vulnerable to reward hacking in multi-objective settings, optimizing only one of the objectives at the cost of the others. It is difficult to obtain high-accuracy reward models in many real-world tasks.

## How MO-GRPO Works

Standard GRPO normalizes after summing rewards, so objectives with larger scale/variance can dominate. MO-GRPO equalizes scales across objectives before aggregation, making optimization less sensitive to reward magnitude mismatch and improving robustness in multi-objective settings.

## Key Benefits

MO-GRPO achieves stable learning by evenly distributing correlations among the components of rewards, outperforming GRPO, showing MO-GRPO to be a promising algorithm for multi-objective reinforcement learning problems.

## Experimental Scope

The paper evaluates MO-GRPO experimentally in four domains: the multi-armed bandits problem, simulated control task (Mo-Gymnasium), machine translation tasks on the WMT benchmark (En-Ja, En-Zh), and instruction following task.

The paper was submitted on September 26, 2025, with a second version on January 9, 2026. A GitHub repository with implementations is available at CyberAgentAILab/MO-GRPO.

I found comprehensive information about the Logic-LM paper. Here's what I found:

## Overview

Logic-LM is a novel framework that integrates LLMs with symbolic solvers to improve logical problem-solving. While LLMs have shown human-like reasoning abilities, they still struggle with complex logical problems.

## Publication Details

The paper was published in the Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023 in Singapore. The authors are Liangming Pan, Alon Albalak, Xinyi Wang, and William Wang.

## Methodology

The method first utilizes LLMs to translate a natural language problem into a symbolic formulation. Afterward, a deterministic symbolic solver performs inference on the formulated problem. The framework also introduces a self-refinement module, which utilizes the symbolic solver's error messages to revise symbolic formalizations.

## Results

Logic-LM's effectiveness was demonstrated on five logical reasoning datasets: ProofWriter, PrOntoQA, FOLIO, LogicalDeduction, and AR-LSAT. On average, Logic-LM achieves a significant performance boost of 39.2% over using LLM alone with standard prompting and 18.4% over LLM with chain-of-thought prompting.

## Availability

Code and data are publicly available.

## Overview

FoVer (First-order logic Verification) is an automated pipeline that verifies the logical correctness of reasoning texts using first-order logic.

## Motivation and Problem

Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in various tasks, including logical reasoning. However, their propensity for generating incorrect or inconsistent responses remains a significant concern.

The pipeline operates in two main steps: (1) LLM-driven translation of natural language into executable logical expressions, and (2) automated logical verification using the Z3 theorem prover.

## Overview

LogiQA is a comprehensive dataset designed to assess an LLM's logical reasoning capabilities, encompassing various types of deductive reasoning, including categorical and disjunctive reasoning. It features 8,678 multiple-choice questions, each paired with a reading passage.

## Data Source

LogiQA is derived from publicly available logical comprehension questions from China's National Civil Servants Examination. The dataset is collected from the Chinese Civil Service Entrance Examination.

## LogiQA 2.0 (2023)

LogiQA 2.0 is an improved dataset for logical reasoning in natural language understanding, published in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing in 2023. The dataset is an amendment and re-annotation of LogiQA in 2020, and the authors increased the data size, refined the texts with manual translation by professionals, and improved the quality by removing items with distinctive cultural features like Chinese idioms.

## Use in LLM Evaluation

LogiQA is widely used as a benchmark for evaluating logical reasoning capabilities in large language models. Earlier datasets like LogiQA and ReClor combine logical reasoning with commonsense reasoning. The benchmark has been employed in various research contexts to assess how well LLMs handle deductive and logical reasoning tasks.

## Overview

DeepSeek-R1 demonstrates that the reasoning abilities of large language models can be incentivized through pure reinforcement learning, removing the need for human-annotated demonstrations.

## Key Technical Details

**GRPO Algorithm**: DeepSeek-R1 uses DeepSeek-V3-Base as the base model and employs GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) as the RL framework to improve model performance in reasoning. GRPO was originally proposed to simplify the training process and reduce the resource consumption of proximal policy optimization (PPO), which is widely used in the RL stage of LLMs.

**Training Approach**: The approach directly applies reinforcement learning to the base model without relying on supervised fine-tuning as a preliminary step, allowing the model to explore chain-of-thought for solving complex problems.

## Model Variants

DeepSeek-R1-Zero, a model trained via large-scale reinforcement learning without supervised fine-tuning as a preliminary step, demonstrated remarkable performance on reasoning. However, DeepSeek-R1-Zero encounters challenges such as endless repetition, poor readability, and language mixing.

To address these issues, DeepSeek-R1 incorporates cold-start data before RL and achieves performance comparable to OpenAI-o1 across math, code, and reasoning tasks.

## Performance

The pass@1 score on AIME 2024 increases from 15.6% to 71.0%, and with majority voting, the score further improves to 86.7%, matching the performance of OpenAI-o1.

## Key Distinctions

Process-supervised Reward Models deliver dense, step-level rewards to guide LLM reasoning, while traditional outcome reward models provide feedback only on the final model output, creating a sparse credit assignment problem.

## Recent Findings and Developments

**Training Data and Challenges:**
PRMs emerge as a promising approach for process supervision in mathematical reasoning of Large Language Models, which aim to identify and mitigate intermediate errors, though their development faces significant challenges, particularly in data annotation and evaluation methodologies.

Commonly used Monte Carlo estimation-based data synthesis for PRMs typically yields inferior performance and generalization compared to LLM-as-a-judge and human annotation methods, as MC estimation relies on completion models to evaluate current-step correctness, leading to inaccurate step verification.

**Novel Approaches:**

**Test-Time Applications:**
In test-time scaling, PRMs function as verifiers or critics, scoring each candidate in a set of independently generated solutions, with output selection based on maximizing aggregate step- or token-level reward, outperforming outcome-only ranking or self-consistency selection.

The research landscape in 2024-2025 shows a shift toward more sophisticated PRM training methods and hybrid approaches that combine multiple verification strategies.

## Overview

LLMorpheus presents a technique where the quality of a test suite is evaluated by introducing faults into a program and determining whether the program's tests detect them.

## Key Innovation

The technique introduces placeholders at designated locations in a program's source code and prompts a Large Language Model (LLM) to suggest what they could be replaced with. This is a departure from traditional approaches, as most existing mutation testing approaches involve applying a fixed set of mutation operators (e.g., replacing a "+" with a "-"), but certain types of real-world bugs cannot easily be simulated by such approaches, limiting their effectiveness.

## Implementation and Evaluation

The technique is implemented in LLMorpheus, a mutation testing tool for JavaScript, and evaluated on 13 subject packages, considering several variations on the prompting strategy, and using several LLMs.

## Results

LLMorpheus is capable of producing mutants that resemble existing bugs that cannot be produced by StrykerJS, a state-of-the-art mutation testing tool. The researchers report on the running time, cost, and number of mutants produced by LLMorpheus, demonstrating its practicality.

## Publication

The article has been accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering with DOI 10.1109/TSE.2025.3562025.

**ArXiv ID:** 2502.18770  
**Authors:** Jiayi Fu, Xuandong Zhao, Chengyuan Yao, Heng Wang, Qi Han, and Yanghua Xiao  
**Latest Version:** January 21, 2026

### Overview

The paper addresses how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) is essential for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values, but RLHF is susceptible to reward hacking, where the agent exploits flaws in the reward function rather than learning the intended behavior, thus degrading alignment.

### Key Contributions

The paper presents a comprehensive study of the prevalent reward shaping methods, with analysis suggesting two key design principles: (1) the RL reward should be bounded, and (2) the RL reward benefits from rapid initial growth followed by gradual convergence.

Guided by these insights, they propose Preference As Reward (PAR), a novel approach that leverages the latent preferences embedded within the reward model as the signal for reinforcement learning.

### Experimental Results

The authors evaluated PAR on the base model Gemma2-2B using two datasets, Ultrafeedback-Binarized and HH-RLHF, with experimental results demonstrating PAR's superior performance over other reward shaping methods. On the AlpacaEval 2.0 benchmark, PAR achieves a win rate of at least 5 percentage points higher than competing approaches.

Furthermore, PAR exhibits remarkable data efficiency, requiring only a single reference reward for optimal performance, and maintains robustness against reward hacking even after two full epochs of training.

## LoRP: LLM-based Logical Reasoning via Prolog

LoRP is a hybrid reasoning framework combining LLMs and Prolog. The framework utilizes LLMs to convert natural language queries into Prolog code, and delegates reasoning to the external SWI-Prolog interpreter.

### Key Components

A systematic FOL-to-Prolog translation mechanism extends Prolog's expressiveness. LoRP decouples language understanding and symbolic inference via four reasoning stages. 

The framework includes several operational steps:
- A syntax validator assesses the translated Prolog code for completeness and correctness
- The validated Prolog code is executed using an external interpreter, SWI-Prolog, to derive reasonings
- A three-vote majority mechanism is implemented where each query is independently processed three rounds, and the most frequent result is selected as the final output

### Performance and Advantages

Extensive experiments show LoRP achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that LoRP significantly improves LLMs' reasoning performance, particularly as inference depth increases.

### Publication

This research was published in Knowledge-Based Systems in July 2025.

## Overview of RLVR

Verifiable Rewards are simple functions that provide a clear-cut, binary ground truth signal - typically a "1" (correct) or "0" (incorrect) - to indicate whether a model's output meets a predefined correctness criterion. Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards is among the leading training strategies for injecting learning signals into LLMs, successfully employed by models such as DeepSeek R1 and Tülu 3.

## Code Execution and Formal Correctness

In scenarios where LLMs are used to generate code, verifiable rewards are derived from executing the code and comparing the outcome to an expected result: unit tests, exceptions etc. In the multi-turn code synthesis setup, verifiable rewards can be assigned based on the execution results of generated code against test cases. Code generation provides natural verification through execution. Partial rewards can be awarded when code compiles and runs without errors, while full rewards are achieved when outputs pass comprehensive unit tests.

## Structured Feedback and Verification

Designing a verifiable reward function requires expert knowledge, domain expertise, and structured data interfaces. This ensures reinforcement learning (RL) systems optimize for measurable, high-quality outputs while avoiding biases and misalignments. RLVRR (reinforcement learning with verifiable reference-based rewards) is a framework that extends RLVR to open-ended generation. Instead of relying on a single verifiable dot, RLVRR extracts an ordered sequence of verifiable linguistic signals from high-quality references, transforming the dot supervision into a reward chain.

## Recent 2024-2025 Research

Recent research from 2025 has explored the mechanisms behind RLVR effectiveness. Recent advancements in long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, particularly through the Group Relative Policy Optimization algorithm used by DeepSeek-R1, have led to significant interest in the potential of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for Large Language Models. RLVR can extend the reasoning boundary for both mathematical and coding tasks.

## FOLIO: Natural Language Reasoning with First-Order Logic

FOLIO is a human-annotated, logically complex and diverse dataset for reasoning in natural language (NL), equipped with first-order logic (FOL) annotations.

### Dataset Details

FOLIO consists of 1,430 examples (unique conclusions), each paired with one of 487 sets of premises used to deductively reason for the validity of each conclusion. The logical correctness of the premises and conclusions is ensured by their FOL annotations, which are automatically verified by an FOL inference engine.

### Key Features

In addition to the main NL reasoning task, NL-FOL pairs in FOLIO constitute a new NL-FOL translation dataset. The dataset is notable for its complexity and diversity, with the mode of reasoning depths being four in FOLIO, and 28.7% of the examples needing five or more depths of reasoning to infer the conclusions.

### Publication and Authors

The paper was authored by Simeng Han and 34 other authors, and was published to arXiv in 2022 (paper ID 2209.00840).

### Results

A subset of FOLIO presents a challenge for one of the most capable Large Language Models (LLMs) publicly available, GPT-4.

## The Coupling Effect Hypothesis

The coupling effect hypothesizes that test data sets that detect simple types of faults are sensitive enough to detect more complex types of faults. More specifically in the context of mutation testing, complex mutants are coupled to simple mutants in such a way that a test data set that detects all simple mutants in a program will also detect a large percentage of the complex mutants.

## Offutt's Empirical Validation

Offutt provided experiments in support of the hypothesis showing that the vast majority of the higher-order mutants are coupled to the first-order mutants. All the results from this investigation support the validity of the coupling effect, with the major conclusion being that by explicitly testing for simple faults, we are also implicitly testing for more complicated faults.

## Key Empirical Evidence

Test data developed to kill 1st-order mutants killed over 99% of 2nd-order and 3rd-order mutants, which implied that the mutation coupling effect hypothesis is valid. Additionally, the overall results indicate that the hypothesis of a coupling effect is largely valid, provided the program is not too large; only a tiny proportion of higher-order mutants is expected to survive a test set that kills all first-order mutants.

## Overview

NL2FOL is a framework to autoformalize natural language to First-Order Logic (FOL) step by step using Large Language Models (LLMs). The goal is to translate natural language into formal language such as First-Order Logic, which is a foundational challenge in NLP with wide-ranging applications in automated reasoning, misinformation tracking, and knowledge validation.

## Approach and Methodology

The framework designs a process to reliably detect logical fallacies by translating natural language to First-order Logic (FOL) step-by-step using Large Language Models. By leveraging structured representations generated by NL2FOL, the approach uses Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) solvers to reason about the logical validity of natural language statements.

## Key Features

Being neurosymbolic, the approach provides interpretable insights into the reasoning process and demonstrates robustness without requiring model fine-tuning or labeled training data. The model also provides a novel means of utilizing LLMs to interpret the output of the SMT solver, offering insights into the counter-examples that illustrate why a given sentence is considered a logical fallacy.

## Performance Results

On the LOGIC dataset, NL2FOL achieves an F1-score of 78%, while generalizing effectively to the LOGICCLIMATE dataset with an F1-score of 80%. The approach is able to generalize effectively, achieving an F1-score of 73% on the challenge set, LogicClimate, outperforming state-of-the-art models by 21% despite its much smaller size.

papers:

  # ============================================================
  # Category 1: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
  # ============================================================

  - id: deepseek-r1
    title: "DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "DeepSeek-AI"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv 2501.12948 / Nature 2025"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: method-component
    relevance: >
      Demonstrates that pure RL (GRPO) can incentivize reasoning in LLMs without SFT.
      STA builds on the same GRPO framework but replaces binary outcome reward with
      intensional structural reward for neurosymbolic formalization.
    key_finding: >
      DeepSeek-R1-Zero trained via GRPO alone achieves 71% on AIME 2024,
      showing emergent chain-of-thought reasoning from RL alone.

  - id: deepseekmath
    title: "DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models"
    authors: "Zhihong Shao, Peiyi Wang, Qihao Zhu, Runxin Xu, et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv 2402.03300"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: method-component
    relevance: >
      Introduces GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization), the RL algorithm
      used in STA training. GRPO eliminates the critic model by estimating
      baselines from group scores.
    key_finding: >
      GRPO matches PPO performance while significantly reducing training
      resources; improves GSM8K 82.9->88.2% and MATH 46.8->51.7%.

  - id: logic-rl
    title: "Logic-RL: Unleashing LLM Reasoning with Rule-Based Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "Xian et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv 2502.14768"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: direct-competitor
    relevance: >
      Uses rule-based RL (REINFORCE++) for LLM logical reasoning on synthetic
      logic puzzles. Closest competitor to STA's approach of RL for logical
      formalization, though Logic-RL uses extensional (answer-correctness)
      rewards rather than STA's intensional structural rewards.
    key_finding: >
      REINFORCE++ outperforms GRPO on logic puzzles with superior stability;
      rule-based reward design is critical for RL-based logical reasoning.

  - id: mellgren-prolog-grpo
    title: "Training Language Models to Use Prolog as a Tool"
    authors: "Niklas Mellgren"
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv 2512.07407"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: direct-competitor
    relevance: >
      Uses GRPO to train a 3B LLM to generate Prolog code for reasoning,
      directly comparable to STA's approach of GRPO-training a formalizer.
      Key difference: uses pass/fail reward vs STA's structural ISR.
    key_finding: >
      GRPO is effective for teaching small LLMs to use Prolog as a tool
      for logical and mathematical reasoning.

      verified by SAT solver. Similar pipeline to STA (LLM->formal spec->solver)
      but uses prompting, not RL training.
